title: 2 Peter Bible Quiz - Chapter 2
description: Ten questions on 2 Peter 2: false teachers, the examples of Noah and Lot, and the way of Balaam.

questions.text: What will the false teachers secretly bring in, according to verse 1?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 says false teachers will secretly bring in destructive heresies, denying even the Master who bought them.

questions.text: How will they exploit people in their covetousness?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says that in covetousness they will exploit you with deceptive words.

questions.text: Who was preserved when God brought a flood on the world of the ungodly?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says God didn't spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah with seven others, a preacher of righteousness.

questions.text: Which cities does verse 6 say were turned into ashes?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says God turned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes, making them an example to those who would live in an ungodly way.

questions.text: Who is called righteous and was distressed by the lustful life of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 say God delivered righteous Lot, who was very distressed by the lustful life of the wicked.

questions.text: What does verse 11 say angels do not do, though they are greater in might and power?
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says that angels, though greater in might and power, don't bring a railing judgment against them before the Lord.

answers.text: Speak of the day of judgment
Bring a railing judgment against them
Look into the things of men

questions.text: Whose way did they follow when they forsook the right way?
questions.explanation: Verse 15 says that forsaking the right way, they went astray, having followed the way of Balaam the son of Beor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing.

questions.text: What stopped the madness of the prophet, according to verse 16?
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says a mute donkey spoke with a man's voice and stopped the madness of the prophet.

questions.text: What do they promise, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption?
questions.explanation: Verse 19 says they promise them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption.

questions.text: What proverb does verse 22 say has happened to them?
questions.explanation: Verse 22 quotes the true proverb: the dog turns to his own vomit again, and the sow that has washed to wallowing in the mire.

answers.text: The dog turns to his own vomit
The tree is known by its fruit
